title: Aftershock zones of 60 shallow Japanese mainshocks (JMA, Mj 5.0-7.6, 1998-2024) grew by 0.15 rupture lengths per tenfold time; static-kernel ETAS cascades gave 37-69% of this
abstract: We tested whether aftershock zones grow with time beyond catalog artifacts and cascades of aftershocks. We used the JMA hypocenter catalog for 1998-2024. We selected isolated shallow (20 km or less) Japanese mainshocks of Mj 5.0-7.6. We kept events of magnitude Mmain-3 or more from 0.03 days. This floor was complete in the stacked data. For 60 sequences, a median regression of epicentral distance over rupture length L on log10(time) gave a mean slope of 0.146 L per decade (95% bootstrap interval 0.088-0.217). The median slope was 0.073, and 47 of 60 slopes were positive. Six other floors, start times and background rules gave means of 0.120-0.175. Growth in km per decade scaled as L^1.01. ETAS cascades with static spatial kernels, measured with the same code, gave mean slopes of 0.054-0.101 for branching ratios 0.5-0.8. This is 37-69% of the observed mean. The observed mean was above all simulated means for branching ratios 0.5-0.6 (p < 0.01), but not clearly above them for 0.8 (p = 0.09). An extreme set with branching ratio 0.9 gave the full mean, but it matched the data poorly. After nearest-neighbour thinning to mainshock-linked events, the observed mean of 0.115 stayed above three of four null sets. The excess came from a minority of sequences: 7-12 of about 55 were above their own null 95th percentile, and the median sequence was not clearly above most nulls. In a post hoc test, sequences with raised activity in the 30 days before the mainshock had a larger excess (Mann-Whitney p = 0.002-0.011). The largest excesses were in known swarm areas (Hida-Kamikochi, Izu). Log-time and square-root-time growth fitted equally well. A heat-flow link was not robust to the averaging radius. Limitations: the ETAS parameters were not fitted to the sequences, distances are from the epicenter with a scaling-law rupture length, catalogs are not relocated, many sequences are small, and the exploratory tests have no multiple-test correction. Code, per-sequence and per-simulation tables, and figures are included. Raw catalogs remain external.
